editorial.headline: Food and Drink Packing: Open Nationally, Clear in Bali at Higher Risk
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers contract packing for processed food and drink materials and products, with full foreign ownership available nationally and no Bali moratorium block at large scale.
editorial.body:
This is the business of packing processed food and drink materials and products for a fee or under contract. The work may be carried out through automated systems or by hand, but its commercial centre is the same: preparing another party’s food or beverage goods for their next stage of distribution or sale. It includes bottling liquids, including beverages and foods; packing solid items through formats such as blister packs or aluminium-foil wrapping; labelling and stamping; and product sterilisation where it relates to packing. Other related packing work for processed food and drink materials and products also falls within the activity.

The scope is broad enough to accommodate a practical production-service operation rather than one narrow packaging technique. A business can handle liquid bottling alongside solid-goods packing, labelling, stamps, and packing-related sterilisation, provided the work remains directed to processed food and beverage materials or products. The record describes this as paid or contract work, which is an important distinction: the activity is defined by carrying out the packaging service itself, whether the process is automated or manual.

Registration is open at every listed enterprise scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. Nationally, the PMA position is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, the national record permits full foreign ownership for this activity. That national openness is supported by Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, and it applies alongside the available scale range rather than being confined in the record to a single class of enterprise.

Bali requires a more careful reading, but the result here is not a prohibition. The province has an island-wide, permanent moratorium blocking low- and medium-low-risk KBLI activities for PMA. For this activity, however, the OSS risk at the Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. The Bali record therefore marks it OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and states that it is not blocked by the moratorium. A PMA registration in Bali is consequently not barred on that moratorium basis where the activity is assessed at the stated large-scale, higher-risk level.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, full foreign ownership is open; in Bali, the activity is not blocked by the PMA moratorium at the stated large-scale, higher-risk level.
